title: Build bee herding status with the transport probe
action: In herding.rs try_native add "status" => Some(status(rest)). status(flags): accept --main-root and --json; build the same object interlock builds (enabled, marker, main_root, reason) by factoring the marker check out of interlock into fn enable_marker_state(explicit) -> Map; then add transport: {ready: bool, reason: string, pane_id: string|null} from std::env HERDR_ENV=='1' && HERDR_PANE_ID non-empty. Exit 0 always (status is a report, not an interlock). Without --json print one line: 'herding: enabled=<b> transport=<ready|not ready> (<reason>)'. In registry_payload.json remove the unavailable object from the herding.status entry and add --main-root to its parameters (tests/registry_contracts.rs pins shape — run it). Add a unit test for the transport object with both env states via a small fn taking a closure for env lookup.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee herding registry
acceptance: bee herding status --json prints {enabled, marker, main_root, reason, transport:{ready, reason, pane_id}} and exits 0; the not-built message is gone for this verb; herding and registry tests green.
